title: Our Poems Cannot
text:
Our poems cannot

be published yet


They circulate from hand to hand

in manuscript


Or copied on mimeograph

but one day


the name will be forgotten

of the dictator against whom

they were written,


And they will go on being read.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the contrast between clandestine circulation and the poems' longer life beyond the dictator.

title: You Are Alone
text:
You are alone

among the crowds


as alone as

the moon is


And only the sun

in the sky


yesterday you were in the stadium


among thousands of people

and I spotted you from

the moment I came in


just as if you had

been alone

in an empty stadium
editorial_note: The translation keeps the beloved's singularity visible even inside a crowd.

title: Take Care, Claudia
text:
Take care, Claudia,

when you are with me,


because the slightest gesture,

any word, a sigh


from Claudia,

the smallest carelessness,


perhaps one day

scholars will examine it


And this dance of Claudia's

will be remembered for centuries


Claudia, I am warning you now.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the playful warning that intimacy may become literary evidence.

title: Not with Jewels
text:
Not with jewels

from Morlock Jewelers


nor with perfumes

from Dreyfus


nor with orchids

inside their

music box


nor with a Cadillac


but only

with my poems

did I win her


And she prefers me,

though I am poor,

to all of


Somoza's millions
editorial_note: The translation keeps the catalog of luxury gifts displaced by poems and poverty.

title: Our Love
text:
Our love

was born in May

with malinches in bloom


—When the malinches are in bloom

in Managua—.


Only that month

do they give flowers:

in the others

they give pods

but the malinches

will bloom again

in May


and the love

that went away

will not come back

again.
editorial_note: The translation keeps 'malinches' as the Managua flowering trees whose annual return contrasts with love's non-return.
